messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: calculating SD for secr estimates
parts:
Hi Joanna
The standard error (SE) is shown for each 'real' parameter estimate in the tables at the bottom (e.g. 0.000119 / ha). Is that not what you want? If not, what do you mean by standard deviation? (The 95% CI may be preferable to the SE; the latter are an approximation)
Murray

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: calculating SD for secr estimates
parts: It's the SE that you need. As an aside - this confusion is why some of us refer to it as the relative standard error (RSE) rather than CV (although CV is so entrenched that it crops up even in 'secr'!). You should try derived(fsecr5), which calculates it for you. And when comparing RSE be alert to the effect of details=list(distribution = "binomial") vs "poisson" default. And equivalently derived(..., distribution = "binomial")

Murray
